main_topics.reason: The user came in because a similar deep pelvic ache had returned after surgery and described its link to their period.
The user asked whether another operation was needed so soon and later asked what circumstances might justify one.
The user explored alternatives to surgery, particularly after learning about hormonal options and pelvic floor physiotherapy.
The user said the combined pill had caused low mood and low libido and did not want to take it again.
The user returned to ask whether pain recurring three months after surgery was normal and said the timing felt very quick.
The user engaged with the possibility that pelvic floor muscles could contribute to pain beyond endometriosis itself.
The user welcomed the idea of obtaining the operative note and asked for a concrete next step to discuss with their care team.
The user said they felt defeated after expecting surgery to fix the pain, then described feeling more hopeful.

output.summary: The user asked whether returning cyclical pelvic pain three months after endometriosis surgery meant they needed another operation, and explained they did not want to resume the pill because of its effects on mood and libido. The assistant discussed non-surgical options, other possible pain contributors, obtaining the operative note, and questions for a follow-up; the user said the plan was clear and felt less resigned to repeated surgery.
